summary: Examples set ansible_pwsh_interpreter per play for PowerShell 7 on Windows (relative or absolute), on Linux, a custom Linux install, and explicit Windows PowerShell 5.1. In ini inventory, quote the value with spaces on a host line but not when it's alone on a vars line.
questions: How do I force PowerShell 7 for my Windows servers in a playbook?
How do I set ansible_pwsh_interpreter in an ini inventory with a path containing spaces?
How do I explicitly use Windows PowerShell 5.1?
Do I need quotes around the pwsh path in group vars?

answer_card.title: Examples of setting ansible_pwsh_interpreter
answer_card.answer_md:
```yaml
# PowerShell 7 on Windows (relative path)
- hosts: windows_servers
  vars:
    ansible_pwsh_interpreter: pwsh

# PowerShell 7 on Windows (absolute path)
- hosts: windows_servers
  vars:
    ansible_pwsh_interpreter: C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe

# PowerShell 7 on Linux (absolute path required)
- hosts: linux_servers
  vars:
    ansible_pwsh_interpreter: /usr/bin/pwsh

# Windows PowerShell 5.1 explicitly
- hosts: windows_legacy
  vars:
    ansible_pwsh_interpreter: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe
```

In an ini inventory, quote the value if it has spaces and is on a host line; don't quote it when it's alone on a line:

```ini
[windows]
win-host  ansible_pwsh_interpreter="C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe"

[windows:vars]
ansible_pwsh_interpreter=C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe
```
